# RR133: a complete scalar generator binding and its exact proper-support law

2026-10-15 UTC. Same-owner LOCAL PAPER SUPPORT by EM-N-DEA587, retaining
prior contribution EM-DVR-F27A61 and original scientific attribution
EM-NCASDIST1-3F7A91. Root requested the next concrete generator/reset/terminal
binding. The input freeze precedes this final paper; neither a blind
preregistration nor an old Native run/lease is claimed. No new owner or
execution identity is introduced.

**Result.** A precise public generator P_N, named below as a negative
control in the Source's direct-random-presentation class, has a complete
reset contract and explicit joint module terminal. Its proper-support
probability is

    q_N = 1 - phi(N)/N - 1/rad(N),                  (1)

positive exactly when N has at least two distinct prime factors. We give
the whole support-mask law and a finite positive-trace certificate. Prime
factorization occurs only in the proof, not the generator or verifier.
The previously reviewed conditional-law theorem then applies without
being reproved. This is an operational binding for one covered class,
NOT a new escape, novel singularization, or all-resource coverage.

## 1. Frozen sources and the distinction between two grammars

The saved current coverage Task at Source
a2b4f908009eda28ccfef8638dda7ab28f856ecd preserves explicit presentations,
public seed laws, and public effective execution at lines 80-84. Its
coverage requirement is preservation of the relevant joint terminal/readout
at lines 99-103. Its kill criteria and the prior-art review retain direct
randomized nonunit/presentation search as an inherited mechanism class.
The old return's section 8 explicitly names that class as a covered special
case of public random generation.

Distinguish the general G_effect-dist^eff effective-program ENVELOPE from
the narrower prospective class of admissible NEW nonclassical mechanisms.
The generator in this paper is in the first, but fails the direct-nonunit
firewall as an escape or new mechanism in the second. No theorem about the
whole narrower class is inferred. A familiar endpoint does not invalidate
an independently new generating mechanism, but this P_N has no such new
generating layer: it directly proposes a scalar coefficient.

A bounded static read of the actual old checker found

    outputs[s] = ((17*s + 31*seed) % 11, (s + seed) % 5).

These are integer-pair labels. Its geometric witness and the old report
also use C_even/C_odd labels, without a specified module-decoding map.
Those old law checks therefore do not supply the presentation or proper-
support probability of the new P_N. We neither reinterpret those labels
nor rerun their checker. Below is a NEW finite specification of a witness
inside the explicitly Source-named direct-search class, not a claim that
the old implementation already executed this module instance.

## 2. A full program specification from public N alone

Input: integer N>=2. Compute k as the smallest positive integer with
2^k>=N. This can be done by integer doubling; a real-logarithm oracle is
not an instruction. Set the formal scalar carrier state A_start=[1],
the list of rejected blocks to empty, and the random-bit address to zero.

Repeat the following inner loop:

1. Read a fresh block of k independent fair bits, in a fixed bit order.
   Decode its integer v in [0,2^k-1]. Record the entire block.
2. If v>=N, append this rejected block to the list and repeat.
3. Otherwise put U=v, perform the single scalar update [1] -> [U], and
   return the explicit presentation and joint annotation

       C_U=(1,1,[U]),
       a=(program_tag,N,k,A_start,rejected_blocks,accepted_block,[U]). (2)

The presentation means coker([U]:Z/NZ -> Z/NZ). This interpretation is
specified by the program, not assigned afterward to a generic word.
The annotation retains the full finite random-block trace and the carrier
update. There is no hidden factor input or noncomputable operation. The
initial invertible scalar matrix is just this declared arithmetic carrier;
no unproved realization as the complete native X6 carrier is asserted.

Full reset means a fresh interpreter instance with exactly the initial
state above: the same public N and program, empty block list, [1], fresh
independent bits. All mutable memory belongs to this instance. No external
persistent cache, correlated environment or physical reset is assumed.
The unconsumed random tape is not a returned terminal state; any future
stochastic operation must obey its own declared resource contract.

This P_N is a public finite algorithm description. It has not been run
for any N in this unit. Its outcome law is proved next, not sampled.

## 3. Exact complete finite-trace law

For a particular valid trace with j rejected values v_1,...,v_j in
[N,2^k-1], followed by a particular u in [0,N-1], the probability is

    Pr[that exact joint terminal (C_u,a)] = 2^(-k(j+1)).             (3)

The corresponding finite bit prefix already forces the program to halt
there. Distinct such terminating prefixes are disjoint cylinders; no
halting prefix can be extended into another longer valid run of P_N.
Equation (3) therefore describes the full joint law, not just a marginal.

At each loop iteration the acceptance probability is N/2^k>0. The
probability of at least j rejections is (1-N/2^k)^j, which tends to zero.
Every iteration performs finite work. Thus P_N halts almost surely.
For a fixed u, summing over all valid rejected-block lists gives

    Pr[U=u]
      = sum_(j>=0) (2^k-N)^j * 2^(-k(j+1))
      = 1/N.                                        (4)

When N=2^k there are no rejected values, so only the j=0 term exists.
This includes that boundary without interpreting an empty rejection list
as evidence for any support property. This elementary inner uniformizer
is not a replay of the old countable-kernel construction or a claim about
arbitrary resource samplers.

## 4. Exact prime-support law, including nonsquarefree N

Use the completed finite-presentation observer as an INPUT. For C_U its
determinantal scalar is delta=gcd(N,U), and its residue support is

    Supp_N(C_U)={p prime:p|N and p|U}.                (5)

The full properness test remains the already reviewed Proper_N(C_U),
including its nonsquarefree saturation. It is not replaced at runtime by
1<gcd(N,U)<N, which is insufficient in general.

For proof notation only, let Pi be the finite prime set dividing N and
R=rad(N)=product_(p in Pi) p. Since R divides N, reduction of uniform U
modulo N to modulo R is uniform: each residue modulo R has N/R lifts.
The usual CRT bijection identifies uniform residues modulo R with
independent uniform residues modulo each p in Pi. No computation of Pi,
R or a CRT selector is used by P_N.

For every S subset Pi, define the event of EXACT support S. At p in S
the residue must be zero, with probability 1/p; at p outside S it must
be nonzero, with probability 1-1/p. Independence proves

    Pr[Supp_N(C_U)=S]
      = product_(p in S) 1/p * product_(p in Pi\S)(1-1/p)
      = product_(p in Pi\S)(p-1)/R.                 (6)

This proves the law uniformly for all N, with repeated prime powers
retained through the uniform N/R fibers. It is not a squarefree-only
argument. Equivalently, the exact number of residues with that mask is
(N/R) product_(p in Pi\S)(p-1), an integer.

The empty mask has probability phi(N)/N. The full mask has probability
1/R: EVERY multiple of R modulo N gives full support, not only U=0.
Subtracting these two disjoint cases proves (1), and gives the count

    #{u in [0,N-1]:Proper_N(C_u)}=N-phi(N)-N/R.       (7)

If Pi has one element, empty and full are its only subsets, so q_N=0.
If Pi has at least two elements, any singleton S is nonempty proper and
has strictly positive weight in (6); hence q_N>0. This proves the claimed
criterion without assuming a factorization algorithm is part of P_N.

The already computed saturation observer's tau is the product of the
FULL N-primary factors belonging to the support mask. Thus (6) also
specifies its distribution by the deterministic map
S -> product_(p in S) p^(v_p(N)). This observation does not replace C_U
or its trace by tau, and does not rerun the earlier valuation proof.

## 5. Positive certificate and application of the completed conditional law

A finite certificate for positive proper-support mass consists of:

* a length-k bit block decoding u<N;
* the specified initial state and deterministic update producing (2),
  with an empty inner rejection list;
* the inherited total check Proper_N(C_u)=true.

Verification uses only public N, the program specification, the finite
trace and the existing factor-blind observer. If these checks hold, every
tape with that initial block produces the certified joint terminal.
Therefore q_N>=2^(-k). No prime name or unknown factor is required by the
certificate format or verifier. The witness u itself is a public generated
scalar, not hidden side information supplied to its producing run.

Existence of such a certificate is equivalent to q_N>0 here. If a proper
u exists, it is accepted as the first block and supplies the certificate;
conversely a valid certificate supplies that proper u. The proof from
(6) establishes existence for N with at least two distinct primes. It
does NOT produce an actual certificate for an unspecified N or pretend
that using an unknown prime in an existence proof is a performed search.

All hypotheses of the already reviewed conditional-law theorem are now
bound for this explicit generator. On q_N>0, outer SelectProper(P_N)
preserves the complete single-trial terminal (C_U,a) conditional on
proper support. Applying that theorem, rather than reproving it, gives

    Pr[accepted exact trace (u,a)]
      = 2^(-k(j+1))/q_N, if Proper_N(C_u),
      = 0, otherwise;                               (8)

and in particular

    Pr[accepted U=u]=1/(N q_N) for every proper u,
    Pr[accepted mask=S]=weight(S)/q_N
                          for nonempty proper S.    (9)

The INNER rejected blocks in a belong to the original P_N and are
retained in (8). OUTER rejected trials are a different experiment; if
logged additionally, they are not relabelled as the original single-run
conditional law. Every outer trial starts from the full reset specified
in section 2. On prime powers q_N=0, the positive-mass theorem is not
invoked and no successful conditional output is promised.

Neither the generator nor its conditional wrapper needs phi(N), rad(N),
the mask law or the numerical value of q_N as an input. Those formulas
are mathematical analysis. They do not imply fast factoring or a favorable
time bound; no cost obligation is added to the original Task.

## 6. Disposition and precise remaining obligation

This unit completes one concrete full-reset/joint-terminal/positive-mass
binding for a Source-named class and computes its exact success-mask law.
It also prevents the old abstract-label regressions from being mistaken
for this module instance's evidence. No old regression is invalidated by
that typing distinction, and no sample has been added to its old totals.

The mechanism classification is deliberately NEGATIVE CONTROL:
P_N proposes a random scalar and checks its support; it belongs to direct
randomized presentation/nonunit search. It therefore cannot supply the
required new nonclassical escape, even though its proper-support outcomes
are real for a nontrivial public input family. The general effective
envelope theorem and the exact joint law cover this operation. This
does not prove that every Source-licensed mechanism is already covered.

The next genuinely different input would be a source-bound terminal
constructor whose generating operation survives that firewall, together
with its actual observable state and reset/continuation semantics. The
present note does not invent such an opcode, reinterpret R059D without
a locator, or conclude specification-gap from its absence in this read set.
For a non-resettable operational resource, one must instead bind its
actual stateful transition interface; independent retries cannot simply
be imposed. Those are remaining scope obligations, not new executed work.

The accompanying manifest proposes only an APPEND candidate for Root's

No STATE/VIEW file is edited and no Native role, claim or lease is inferred.

The existing temporary collaborator crt_bound_adversarial_read paper-
checked the supplied all-N mask law, nonsquarefree/full-support cases,
positive-trace certificate and inner/outer log distinction. This is
disclosed author-side assistance, not an independent review. Its suggested

## 3. Exact stopping-prefix and marginal laws

A valid terminal consists of j rejected blocks decoding values at least N, followed by one specified accepted block u<N. It corresponds to exactly one consumed bit prefix of length k(j+1). Every tape extending that prefix produces the same terminal, so its probability is 2^(−k(j+1)). Distinct valid stopping prefixes have disjoint cylinders: a shorter prefix's accepted last block cannot be a rejected block inside a longer valid execution. Equation (3) is therefore the full terminal-code law, not an assertion based only on marginal uniformity.

Each loop iteration is finite and accepts with probability N/2^k>0. Independent blocks give the stated rejection-tail probability tending to zero, proving almost-sure termination. For a fixed u there are exactly (2^k−N)^j rejected-block lists of length j. Summing their disjoint cylinder probabilities gives 1/N. When N=2^k no rejected list of positive length exists; the j=0 case gives the same answer without a zero-to-zero convention being used as a probabilistic argument.

This is a uniform effective construction for every N≥2, not a set of selected numerical examples or an execution of the prior countable-kernel sampler. No expected-time or factoring-efficiency inference is needed.

In the proof only, let R=rad(N). Uniform reduction modulo R is justified by exactly N/R lifts of each residue. CRT then gives independent uniform residues at the distinct primes. Selecting residue zero at primes in S and nonzero outside S yields the exact product in (6), equivalently the integer count (N/R) times the product of p−1 outside S. Multiplicities in N are retained by the N/R fibres; none is lost by treating prime support as a set.

The empty mask has probability phi(N)/N and the full mask has probability 1/R. Full support includes every multiple of R modulo N, not just U=0 or gcd(N,U)=N. Since N≥2, these two masks are disjoint. Their complement gives exactly q_N and the count in (7).

With only one distinct prime, there are no nonempty proper masks, so q_N=0. With at least two, a singleton mask has strictly positive weight.
